newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian politician defends naked swim.
newsitem.headline: Australian politician defends naked swim.

text.p: An Australian politician, elected on a platform of promoting family values, said on Wednesday there was nothing wrong with him swimming naked with his girlfriend and six-year-old son in a parliamentary pool.

Tabloid newspaper posters around Sydney on Wednesday screamed "MP In Naked Romp" and "Naked in the house", as local media reported the night last year when Alan Corbett was caught by a security guard swimming naked in a private members' pool.
But Corbett, a member of the New South Wales state parliament, defended his action, saying he was not ashamed of nudity within the family.

"I think its very important that children grow up with a healthy body image, a healthy self image, that they're not ashamed or fearful or afraid of their own sexuality and their own body," Corbett said.
He told reporters he decided to strip only when he arrived at the pool and found his girlfriend and son swimming naked.
"I thought, 'Oh well, what the heck, I'll join them'," Corbett said. "I knew that there was a sign saying you should be appropriately dressed."
A sign requiring MPs to "wear appropriate clothing at all times" was erected in the parliamentary pool area in 1987 after another politician swam naked.
